analysis:
This PR changes only the provider-side reconnect timing and adds close-code diagnostics on the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002).

What changed:
- CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift runLoop (head 12-53) replaces ExponentialBackoff(1s, 30s max) with an injectable CoordinatorReconnectPolicy. A fresh CoordinatorSessionRecorder is created per attempt. The delay is TimeInterval.random(in: policy.nextDelayRange(after: end)). policy.reset() is still called only after a clean return.
- The session is marked opened after sendRegistration (head 157-165).
- The receive callback records the close code on connectionQueue (head 397-400). It does so before handling a receive error. sentCloseCode (head 492-501) reads the first two payload bytes only when count>=2 and the framework reports nil or noStatusReceived, so the read is bounds-safe.
- The close code feeds only the backoff and the logs (head 33-35). The connection is still torn down on a close frame (head 417-419).
- CoordinatorSessionRecorder (CoordinatorClientState.swift head 509-537) guards its state with an unfair lock.
- CoordinatorClient.swift head 120-141 adds the stored policy and an init parameter whose default is CoordinatorReconnectPolicy().

What is unchanged:
- Registration, the App Attest resume nonce reset per connection (head 106-108, 120-121) and the teardown defer.
- Outbound and chunk binding, and the encryption paths (T-008, T-053).

The close-code input comes from the TLS-authenticated coordinator, which is trusted. The 32 MiB inbound cap is unchanged. No new attack surface or data exposure was identified. The close code and URL appear in logs and telemetry; the URL already did.

Open question for integration: the CoordinatorReconnectPolicy and CoordinatorSessionEnd sources were not supplied. These need checking:
- nextDelayRange should keep a nonzero lower bound and a bounded maximum, so that repeated immediate failures or a coordinator 1012 restart cannot cause a tight reconnect storm. This is an availability concern for A-018 and coordinator load.
- The returned range type must never be empty. TimeInterval.random(in:) on an empty Range traps and would crash the provider.
- Whether reset-on-clean-close combined with a short open duration can still bypass backoff.

No regression was found in the supplied code.
